name: TuniSL2025
description: We introduce Tunisian Sign Language, a comprehensive and fully annotated image dataset specifically designed for TSL recognition. This dataset aims to address the critical lack of high-quality resources available for regional Arabic sign languages, particularly in North Africa. TSL consists of 102 122 JPG images, captured from four different participants performing 32 Arabic alphabet signs and 82 commonly used Tunisian words. The images were collected using a high-resolution smartphone camera from three different angles (front, left, and right) to reflect real-world variability in perspective, lighting conditions, and backgrounds. To ensure consistency and data quality, preprocessing steps such as resizing, noise reduction, and image normalization were applied to all samples. The dataset includes both static hand gestures (for alphabet signs) and body-involved gestures (for vocabulary words), providing a rich and diverse visual representation of TSL. Each sign was performed by at least two different individuals, enhancing gesture diversity and making the dataset suitable for training robust machine learning and deep learning models. TSL is intended to serve as a benchmark for researchers and developers working on sign language recognition, computer vision, and assistive technologies. By making this dataset publicly available, we aim to promote inclusive AI development and facilitate communication accessibility for the deaf and hard-of-hearing community across the Arabic-speaking world.
evaluation_method: accuracy (top-1) and F1 for class-balanced performance
reputation: A recently introduced, domain-specific sign-language dataset with limited but growing interest in regional SL research communities.
notes: Non-LLM vision benchmark; performance sensitive to signer variation, lighting, and whether input is image vs video; likely modest dataset size and potential class imbalance.
